getRetentionCohorts.description: Builds the cohort retention grid (Phase 2) Cohort = the company-local month of a client's first service activation (approximated by the earliest services.date_added among services that ever left the pending states). Retention is read at monthly anchors: the last completed snapshot of each company-local calendar month, whose per-service rows are kept forever by the pruning policy. A cohort member counts as retained at an anchor when they hold positive contracted MRR in any currency (client counts are currency-agnostic per the metric contract and are never summed across currency rows). snapshot.description: Runs a full snapshot for the given company for the given company-local date. The workflow is: 1. Acquire a per-company advisory lock (returns false immediately if held). 2. Mark an analytics_snapshot_runs row 'running' for the date. 3. Build analytics_service_mrr rows set-based, chunked by service id. 4. In a single transaction, replace the date's rollup/movement/revenue/fx/ forecast rows and mark the run 'completed'. 5. Prune per-retention old per-service rows (monthly last row kept forever). On any failure the run is marked 'failed', previously completed snapshots are left untouched, and false is returned.

getCompanyAwareUrl.description: Returns a host-relative click target for a staff notification that lands on the right page. A logged-in staff member's company is resolved from the session (blesta_company_id), not the request hostname (AppController::getCompany()), so admins typically work from a single hostname and switch companies in place. We therefore keep notification links on the *current* browser host by returning the stored URL's path only (dropping the company's configured hostname, which AppController::baseUrl() bakes into the stored absolute URL). For a notification that belongs to a different company than the one currently active, the path is routed through the admin company switcher (`login/index/{company_id}/?uri={path}`); admin_login.php writes the requested company to the session then redirects to the path, which redirect() re-anchors to the current HTTP_HOST. For the active company the bare path is returned. Anything that isn't one of our own admin-area URLs (non-staff recipient, missing URL, non-http scheme, dot-segment traversal, or a non-admin path) returns the raw stored URL unchanged.

getCliPhpBinary.description: Returns a PHP CLI binary path suitable for launching the upgrader and for running DB migrations from inside it. Prefers PHP_BINARY when the current SAPI is CLI-capable; falls back to `php` on PATH when PHP_BINARY resolves to an FPM/CGI binary that can't execute a plain script. The fallback is resolved to an absolute path where possible so the upgrader can validate it as an existing executable. The same value is used for the background launch, the manual recovery command, and the job file's php_binary field, so all three code paths behave identically.

getExpectedDatabaseVersion.description: Walks an upgrade mappings file to determine the database_version that should be reached after upgrading from $from_version up to $to_version. The expected end-state is not always equal to $to_version: not every release introduces schema changes, so for example file version 5.13.6 has no DB tasks beyond 5.13.2 and the database_version setting legitimately stops at 5.13.2 even after a successful upgrade to 5.13.6. Used by the upgrader to verify after the migration runs that the database actually advanced to where it should have, catching partial completion and silent extension-failure cases.

isLockActive.description: Reports whether an upgrade lock is currently active and not stale. Intended for callers (like cron) that only need a yes/no answer for "should I avoid running because an upgrade is in progress?". A stale lock counts as inactive — it must be cleared explicitly via clearlock.

launchUpgrader.description: Launches the standalone upgrader as a background process. The command uses `setsid` to put the child in a new session and redirects all three standard streams, which is what lets the process survive the request finishing. On jailed hosting (CloudLinux CageFS, some PHP-FPM configs) a plain `&` leaves the child in the parent request's process group, and the jail kills the whole group when the request ends — leaving the staging dir populated but no upgrader running. `setsid` is provided by util-linux and is available on any modern Linux host that passes the environment check.

markLockLaunchFailed.description: Marks the lock as "launch failed" so the UI treats it as stale even if the PID recorded in it (the web worker's PID) is still alive. The flag is cleared by the upgrader itself when it starts, so a successful manual recovery transitions the UI back to in-progress automatically. The upgrader and job file paths are persisted alongside the flag so that an admin reloading the upgrade page can still see the manual recovery command — the original AJAX response with that command is only delivered once.
